title: Gilgo
summary: Gilgo is a Babylon barrier-beach placename for an inlet from the ocean to Great South Bay, placed between Oak Island and Jones Beach in the source record.
address_label: Gilgo Beach / Gilgo Inlet area, Town of Babylon, NY
history_content: The Gilgo entry is brief and gives no named person or dated event. Later geographic sources preserve Gilgo, Gilgo Oak Island Beach, and the Gilgo life-saving station as names in the Jones Beach and South Oyster Bay barrier-beach landscape.
translation_content:
No secure translation or etymology is given for Gilgo in the available references. No alternate spelling is listed in the available references.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place-names are a fascinating and unusual way to learn more about your area’s history.”

— Jayne Carroll, Key to English Place-Names (2015), quoted statement, paragraph 5
land_loss_content: Gilgo keeps a short but persistent coastal placename visible on the barrier beach where ocean, bay, inlet, and travel routes meet. Its meaning needs further review, but the name remains part of the shoreline geography Tooker documented.
whereintheworld_content: Tooker places Gilgo between Oak Island and Jones Beach, broadly corresponding to the modern Gilgo Beach and inlet area. Its exact historic extent remains uncertain.
